subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 3: Renewable Energy – Writing: A Formal Request Email
outcomes: Know the parts of a formal email.
Change informal sentences into formal ones.

tf.s: 'Dear Mr Brown' is a formal greeting.
tf.why: Yes, it is polite and formal.

tf.s: The first paragraph of a formal email explains why you are writing.
'We would like to request a visit.' is a polite request.
'Take care' is a formal way to end an email.
'To whom it may concern' can start a formal email.
tf.why: Right, we use it when we do not know the name.

tf.s: 'Give me the information.' is a polite formal request.
tf.why: It is too direct; say 'I would like to request some information.'

tf.s: We use 'would' to make a request polite and indirect.
A writing checklist helps you check that all parts of the email are included.
tf.why: Correct, it helps you find what is missing.

tf.s: A formal email should start with 'Hey there!'.

boxes.q: We ___ like to request a visit.

boxes.why: The phrase is 'To whom it may concern'.

boxes.q: What does the first paragraph explain?
Formal version of 'I need some help.'
o: I would like to request some assistance.

boxes.q: What comes at the end of an email?

o: to make sure all parts are included
boxes.why: A checklist helps you check your work.

hunt.q: Start when no name is known
We would like to ___ a visit

mcq.q: Which is the correct order of a formal email?
o: greeting, purpose, details and request, closing
mcq.why: Start with a greeting and end with a closing.

mcq.q: Which closing should you use in an email to a company manager?
Why do we use 'would' in formal emails?
o: To make the request polite and indirect.

mcq.q: How should a formal email begin?
o: Dear Mr/Ms … or To whom it may concern
I would like to request some information.
mcq.why: 'I would like to request' is polite.

mcq.q: Put in order: like / We / would / to / request / a visit
o: We would like to request a visit.
We like would to request a visit.
Would we like request to a visit.
We would request like to a visit.

mcq.q: Correct the sentence: 'i would like request a visit.'
o: I would like to request a visit.
i would like request a visit.
I like would to request a visit.

mcq.q: Why is 'Can you help with the visit?' not suitable for a formal email?
o: It is too direct and informal.
It is in the past tense.
mcq.why: Formal emails use 'I would like to request…'.

mcq.q: A student writes to a wind farm manager they do not know. Which opening is best?
o: Dear Sir or Madam / To whom it may concern

mcq.q: A partner's plan has a greeting, a purpose and a closing but no visit date. What is the most useful comment?
o: You could add the date of the visit.
mcq.why: Adding details makes the request clear.
